claims.text: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) has an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
Untreated TC4 has low surface hardness.
Untreated TC4 has poor friction and wear performance under high-contact-stress conditions.
Friction stir processing can incorporate pre-placed RHEA particles into a shallow near-surface layer of TC4.
The severe plastic deformation and localized heating of FSP will mix the RHEA particles into TC4.
FSP will form a metallurgical bond between the particle-modified surface and the bulk TC4.
FSP at approximately 1000 rpm and 100 mm/min can produce uniform particle distribution while avoiding excessive thermal exposure.
The intervention will produce a homogeneous dispersion of RHEA particles in the near-surface region.
The FSP-modified near-surface region will be refined and recrystallized.
The intervention will create a graded composite microstructure with robust bonding to the underlying TC4.
Dispersed RHEA particles will strengthen the modified layer through dispersion strengthening.
Grain refinement caused by FSP will contribute to improved wear resistance.
Mechanical interlocking produced by FSP will ensure a strong metallurgical bond.
The composite microstructure and bonded interface will distribute contact stresses and delay abrasion and delamination.
The intervention will increase surface hardness relative to untreated TC4.
The intervention will reduce wear rate relative to untreated TC4 under room-temperature, high-contact-stress testing.
The intervention will not initiate detrimental phases or compromise the ductility and beneficial bulk properties of TC4.
Interfacial reactions and FSP-induced residual stresses may affect the overall performance of the modified TC4.
